one_line_summary: A clean-lined, leather-and-rubber low-top sneaker made in Brazil with ethically sourced materials and a large embroidered V on the side.
energy: considered casual — the sneaker of someone who cares but doesn't want you to notice they care
pull_quote: Buy if you want a white sneaker with some character but minimal sportiness, and the sustainability story matters to you. Pass if you can't get past the big V — it's louder in person than in photos.

verdicts.label: clean / restrained / thoughtful
verdicts.reasoning: The V-10 is the sweet spot between a Common Projects (too precious) and an Adidas Stan Smith (too generic). The wild rubber sole and sustainable materials are real — Veja's supply chain is one of the most transparent in footwear. The leather ages well, the silhouette holds up across seasons, and you'll wear them more than you'd guess.

verdicts.label: clean / structured / restrained
verdicts.reasoning: The V is large. It's not subtle. If your aesthetic is 'no visible branding,' look at the Veja Esplar (smaller V) or the Common Projects Achilles instead. The V-10 was designed to be recognizable; that's a feature for some, a bug for you.

verdicts.label: soft / lived-in / undone
verdicts.reasoning: The V-10 reads slightly fashion-coded — they look 'styled' rather than thrown-on. If your default is actually low-key, an Adidas Samba or a New Balance 530 will sit more naturally in your closet. The V-10 wants to be seen a little.

verdicts.label: performance / durability-first
verdicts.reasoning: The wild rubber sole grips well and the leather is hardier than Common Projects, but the cushioning is minimal — these are fashion sneakers with practical sole, not walking shoes. Fine for 2-3 miles a day; less fine for 6+ or city commuting in wet weather.

why_people_love_it: Genuinely transparent supply chain — organic cotton, agroforestry rubber, traceable leather. Most 'sustainable' sneakers don't hold up to scrutiny; Veja does
The wild rubber sole develops light yellowing over years rather than crumbling — they age into character
Available in non-leather (CWL canvas) versions for $130; same silhouette, no animal products
where_it_falls_flat: Run a half-size large — the toe box is narrow. Order true to size only if you have a slim foot
The white leather creases visibly across the toe within 2 weeks; not damage, but you'll see it
The big V picks up scuffs more visibly than expected; in cream or white, expect noticeable wear by month 6

alternatives.name: Common Projects Achilles Low
alternatives.reasoning: No logo, premium Italian leather, much more expensive. The minimalist version of the same idea.

alternatives.name: Veja Campo CWL
alternatives.reasoning: Same brand, corn-waste-leather upper, slightly different silhouette. $20 cheaper, no animal products, identical sustainability story.

alternatives.name: Adidas Samba OG
alternatives.reasoning: Different aesthetic register entirely — sits more naturally with denim and tees. $50 cheaper. Better if 'I want a casual sneaker' is the actual brief.
